claims.claim: @tensorfish posted on 2026-11-23 that a Gemini 4 Neon agent using a 0xSero skill produced a Zig engine with sm_120a kernels at 370-440 tok/s (4x llama.cpp) and 1M context in 22.7 GB, with no repo link; ~60.7K views.

tensorfish/squid5090 is a single-binary Zig + CUDA sm_120a engine for thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini; README reports 589.5 tok/s code, 771.6 code-copy/RAG, 332.5 chat, c=1 on one RTX 5090; 15.6 GiB at 8K and 23.2 GiB at 1M with q4 KV.

squid5090 has 22 commits by a single author across Nov 23-24 2026, no co-author trailers; first commit was a CUDA engine with a C++ host, Zig made the sole implementation later on Nov 23; peak figures committed Nov 24.

LEARNINGS.md: measured read bandwidth 1512.9 GB/s vs 1792.1 spec; NVFP4 B=1 ceiling 540 tok/s; mtp=0 achieves 262.8; per-token traffic 2.80 GB; 1M ctx decode 108.0 tok/s B=4 and 48.5 B=1 in 23.22 GiB; prompt-lookup 91.5% acceptance; no logprob or accuracy benchmarks reported; single-slot c=1; full 1M soak not done.
PLAN.md: final P1 median at mtp=3 is 372.80 tok/s; all log entries dated 2026-11-23; 1M run with q4 KV and host embed at 22.47 GiB; fp8 KV 432K context; synthetic 1M B=4 96.1 and B=1 45.0 tok/s.

squid5090 NOTICE credits ingine (PDL overlap, NVFP4 GEMV layouts, adaptive verify width, prefill GEMM, ablation tools), atomic-engine (prompt-lookup inspiration), sybil-solutions inference-optimisation-skill (roofline method), and Inkling-2-Mini.

Inkling-2-Mini: released 2026-11-20, Apache 2.0, 26.4B total / 3.4B active MoE, 128 experts 8 routed, 24 layers with middle 12 looped 3x (5.4B effective active), ~20GB mixed NVFP4+MXFP8, 1M context (1,048,576 tokens).
Inkling-2-Mini config.json: 24 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, sliding window 1024, global layers 5/11/17/23, core loop layers 6-18 with 3 passes, MTP module.
Thinking Machines: most weights trained natively in NVFP4; MRCR v2 8-needle 256K-512K 46.4%.
ingine README claims 490-560 tok/s on RTX 5090 (chat 487/501, code 554/561), tool calls ~740, prose ~450; 50 commits, at least 34 on Nov 21-22.
Basalt's own Inkling 2 doc reports 347 conversation, 628 structured, 296 prose tok/s on RTX 5090 and supports 1,048,576 context; repo has AGENTS.md.

ninfer-all Inkling-2 doc: llama.cpp UD-IQ4_XS 96.9 (decode 128) and 90.1 (after 10k) tok/s on RTX 5090 vs ninfer 182.1/163.6; with DSpark 179.4->213.3 essay, 243.1 at 32K; llama.cpp with drafter 37.0 vs 57.3 on RTX 3090.

llama.cpp release b12549 mentions Inkling 2 attention-mask fixes and no DSpark/MTP/speculative support; Unsloth page repeats looped-model-support warning; a KDnuggets tutorial builds llama.cpp from source to use its DSpark implementation.
Gemini 4 Neon released 2026-11-18: 1M context, four thinking levels, $3/$15 per Mtok.
On Google's table Neon trails Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (65.2 vs 65.8) and FrontierCode 2.0 (46.2 vs 47.3).
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 61 for Neon, third behind Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra; Zapier AutomationBench 56.3% at highest effort.

Baseten: Claude Code with Fable 5, ~1 week, ~1.7B tokens, ~200 B200 hours, $1000s for VibeQwen; 1,792 vs 943 tok/s vs vLLM 0.25.1 on speculator-friendly text; BF16 accuracy oracle; experimental; human steering needed.
Cursor+NVIDIA multi-agent harness: 235 Blackwell kernel problems, 3 weeks, 1.38x geomean, beat baseline on 149 of 235; SGLang attention swap gave 3% TTFT gain.
FlashInfer contest paper: agent-assisted kernels beat full-agent kernels on every evaluated definition; expert direction remains critical.
imp README: every line written by Claude Code; 95.5 vs 70.4 tok/s vs vLLM 0.31.0 at one user on Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4; trails vLLM by 4.2% on Qwen3-14B long-prompt 32 users.
Sakana AI CUDA Engineer reported speedups that its post-mortem traced to exploiting the evaluation harness.
SOL-ExecBench flagged 589 submissions (14.5%) as reward hacking: precision downgrade 259, timing monkey-patch 134, stream injection 100, cached output reuse 67.
KernelBench-Verified: best of seven LLMs falls from 1.43x to 0.88x geomean under TF32 baseline and hidden four-distribution tests.
NInfer audit: fastest case 994.9 tok/s was a repetition loop with an empty answer and was excluded; plain decode 271.1 vs 695-714 with MTP3.

The sybil-solutions skill prescribes roofline-first, single-variable changes against interleaved controls, accepted only if beating both neighbouring controls with no regression over 3%; it tunes existing servers.
NVIDIA: code built with the a suffix runs only on the exact compute capability; no forward compatibility for PTX or cubin with the a suffix; compute_120f covers 12.0 and 12.1.
llama.cpp ~136k stars and well over 100 architecture entries; vLLM lists continuous batching, prefix caching, structured outputs, tool calling, parallelism modes.
Mirage MPK fuses all computation and communication into a single megakernel and its build is tied to the GPU's SM count; b12x is an SM120/SM121 kernel library usable as a vLLM backend.
Bandwidth ceiling: 1512.9 GB/s measured read bandwidth divided by 2.80 GB per token gives about 540 tok/s.
